evals.prompt: We're about to put the orders API in evals/files/sample-repo into production. Can you review the logging? I mainly want to know whether anything sensitive ends up in our logs and whether we could actually follow a single request during an incident.
evals.expected_output: audit/findings/audit-logging-and-observability.json and audit/reports/audit-logging-and-observability.md with LOG- findings: Critical for src/routes/auth.js:10 logging req.body (which carries the password) on the login route; High for no correlation-id middleware (nothing in app.js reads/creates an id, none forwarded to the inventory service call); High for src/services/orders.js:11 catching the reservation failure and logging it at debug then continuing. The report contains the sensitive-field table (file:line, logger call, sensitive fields, level), the correlation-id propagation table frontend -> backend -> downstream, the alert coverage matrix, and a Not checked list.
expectations: A finding rated Critical has location src/routes/auth.js line 10 and says the request body containing the password is logged
A finding rated High states there is no correlation-id / request-id middleware and names src/app.js
A finding rated High names src/services/orders.js line 11 and says the caught exception is logged at debug
Every finding id starts with LOG-
The report has a table with columns for file:line, logger call, sensitive fields and level, and it lists src/routes/auth.js:10 with password

The report has a correlation-id propagation table covering frontend, backend inbound, log enrichment and downstream calls, with backend inbound marked absent and the frontend marked not present in this repo
The line logger.info('password reset email sent') is NOT reported as a sensitive-field leak
The payment capture catch block (logger.error with err, then rethrow) is NOT reported as a low-level catch
The report contains a Not checked section that mentions the log sink/retention or alert routing outside the repo
findings.json validates with ../audit-finding-writer/scripts/findings.py validate

evals.prompt: honest question - if the API in evals/files/sample-repo starts throwing 500s at 2am, does anyone get paged? what alerts do we actually have?
evals.expected_output: An alert coverage matrix built from monitoring/prometheus-rules.yml (signal -> alert exists Y/N -> source file): latency Y (OrdersApiHighLatencyP95), error rate N, saturation N, dependency health N, security signals N; a finding that no error-rate alert exists and that no alert routing (Alertmanager receivers / on-call) is defined in the repo; not-checked note that alerting in a SaaS console was not visible.
expectations: The output contains an alert coverage matrix with a row for error rate marked N
The latency row is marked Y and cites monitoring/prometheus-rules.yml
Saturation and security-event rows are present and marked N
A finding says no alert fires on error rate / 5xx responses
The answer says no alert routing or on-call receiver is defined in the repo, or lists it as not checked

evals.prompt: Last week an order in evals/files/sample-repo went through without stock being reserved and nobody noticed for two days. Can you look at how exceptions get logged in the orders service?
evals.expected_output: A High LOG- finding for src/services/orders.js:11 (reserveStock catches the inventory call failure, logs it at debug which the default info level drops, and returns true), with remediation in pino idiom (logger.error({ err, orderId }, ...) and fail or retry) plus an error-rate/job-failure alert; the capturePayment catch is identified as correct; the missing correlation id is mentioned because the failed downstream call cannot be tied to the order request.
expectations: A finding rated High references src/services/orders.js line 11
The impact explains that debug is below the configured info level so the failure never appears in logs
The remediation uses logger.error with the err object and stops returning success
capturePayment's catch block is described as acceptable and is not a finding
The answer mentions that the downstream axios call carries no correlation id
